arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Clement argued the federal law bans prescribing drugs for suicide.
Mr. Atkinson argued states can regulate medical practice responsibly.
Justice Souter questioned if the statute authorizes doctors to prescribe lethal drugs.
Justice O'Connor questioned if a new Attorney General could change the rule.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on the federal Controlled Substances Act. The government claims the law bans prescribing drugs for suicide. Oregon claims the law only regulates drug distribution, not medical practice.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between federal drug regulation and state medical authority. It determines whether federal law overrides state decisions on end-of-life care. The outcome shapes the balance of power between federal and state governments.
